title: I Took the Surfboard-Rack Hours to the Local Who Stacked Five

parts.text: I tagged slot 3 at 6:19 a.m. and local Kade had five boards on a two-board rail. The stencil said: TWO BOARDS. DAYLIGHT HOURS. TAG THE SLOT. I was twenty-seven, permit holder, holding a tag. Kade shrugged. "Locals are the rack." I photographed the stencil, the tag, and the five fins. Then I asked for the rack log. At 6:25 beach ops pinged why Kade's name was on a five-stack. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Beach ops can see Kade's five boards on a two-board rail during my hours.

social.video_title: The local stacked five boards on a two-board rail — Part 1/2
social.description: Surf rack, a daylight stencil, five fins. I logged the stack. Would you have asked beach ops?

parts.text: Kade called it community until ops asked for the still. I printed the log, the stencil, and the photo. Three boards left. Kade ran two and told the next local community was always about optics. Optics is a word locals use when stencils exist. Hours now have a second line: LOCALS ARE NOT THE RAIL. I keep slot 3. Kade brown-bags the jokes. The rack finally looks like a tag, not a shed. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Locals are not the rail — Part 2/2
social.description: Rack log, three boards gone, and a second line. Was community ever five?
